record.original_question: For each positive integer s, is the number f(s) of simultaneous (s, s+1, s+2)-core partitions equal to Σ_{k≥0} binom(s, 2k) C_k, equivalently with generating function (1 − x − √(1 − 2x − 3x^2)) / (2x^2) in the denominator form stated in Conjecture 11.1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.1 Let C_k = 1/(k+1) (2k choose k) be the Catalan number. The number f(s) of (s, s+1, s+2)-cores equals f(s) = Σ_{k≥0} (s choose 2k) C_k.
Conjecture 11.1 through 11.4 have found resolutions and certain extensions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \cdots)$ of a nonnegative integer is called a $t$-core if none of its hook lengths is divisible by $t$. For positive integers $t_1, t_2, \dots, t_r$, a partition is called a simultaneous $(t_1, t_2, \dots, t_r)$-core if it is a $t_i$-core for every $i$. Let $C_k = \tfrac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$ denote the $k$-th Catalan number. For each positive integer $s$, let $f(s)$ denote the number of simultaneous $(s, s+1, s+2)$-core partitions. Prove or disprove the following identity:
$$f(s) \;=\; \sum_{k\ge 0} \binom{s}{2k}\, C_k,$$
equivalently, that the generating function $\sum_{s\ge 0} f(s)\, x^s$ equals $\dfrac{1 - x - \sqrt{1 - 2x - 3x^2}}{2x^2}$ (the generating function for Motzkin numbers, up to the standard shift).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that the number of $(s,s+1,s+2)$-core partitions equals the Motzkin-number sum $\sum_k \binom{s}{2k} C_k$ has been proved. The result is established (with various proofs and extensions, including via bijections to Motzkin paths) by Amdeberhan–Leven and others, and the self-conjugate analogue was settled by Cho–Huh–Sohn (Ramanujan J., 2021).

status_evidence.title: Self-conjugate (s,s+d,…,s+pd)-core partitions and free rational Motzkin paths
status_evidence.snippet: Studies (s,s+1,s+2)-core partitions and connections to Motzkin paths, building on the resolved conjecture that f(s) equals the Motzkin-type sum.
status_evidence.claim: The Motzkin-sum formula for the count of (s,s+1,s+2)-core partitions is established and used as a known result.

status_evidence.title: Simultaneous Core Partitions: Parameterizations and Sums (V. Y. Wang)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys simultaneous core partition enumerations including the (s,s+1,s+2) case proved equal to a Motzkin-type sum.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture about f(s) for (s,s+1,s+2)-cores is treated as a theorem.
